inputs.share_count_basis: 6,081,128,038 ordinary shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim note 17), after the Feb-2026 off-market cancellation of Qatar Airways' 643,076,181 shares. The 2026 convertible bonds matured 5 Feb 2026 (last conversions Jan 2026); the company has no share option or award scheme, so basic = fully diluted. Held flat: no SBC, no planned issuance.
inputs.net_debt_note: Pro forma 31 Dec 2025 net borrowings HK$46,812m (total borrowings 59,101 incl. lease liabilities 26,676, less liquid funds 12,289; FY2025 AR note 11) PLUS the Feb-2026 Qatar Airways buyback HK$6,987m and the FY2025 final dividend HK$3,892m paid in H1 2026. The December balance sheet is used (not June's HK$47,267m) because the flows start with full-year FY2026: pairing a June balance sheet with a full FY2026 flow would count H1 2026 cash generation (~HK$10bn) twice. The June figure reconciles: 57,691 less H1 retained cash generation = 47,267.
inputs.sbc_source: No share option or share award scheme (H1 FY2026 interim note 17: 'The Group has not adopted any share option scheme or share award scheme'). SBC-zero market; SBC rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.buyback_note: Only buyback in the history: one-off HK$6,987m off-market purchase of Qatar Airways' 9.57% stake (HK$10.8374/share) in Feb 2026, treated as a balance-sheet event in the pro forma net debt, not a recurring programme.
inputs.fx_note: Statements are in HK$ (functional currency; US$ columns in the filings are supplementary at 7.8). Quote is HKD on HKEX. No conversion.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:05Z (HKEX regular close, Friday; Yahoo chart API)
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2025-12-31 (pro forma for Feb-2026 buyback and FY2025 final dividend; cross-checked to 2026-06-30 interim)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in HKD, which is pegged to USD: risk-free ~4.0% (10y UST ~4.2%, HKGB 10y ~3.5%), ERP 5.5%, levered airline beta ~1.2 -> cost of equity ~10.6%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (blended loans, MTNs, lease liabilities at amortised cost; FY2025 finance charges 3,169 on ~64bn average borrowings = ~5%), after HK 16.5% tax ~3.8%. Market-value weights ~60% equity / 40% net debt (incl. leases). WACC ~8.1%, rounded up to 8.5%. The extra ~0.4pp is for the ~20.5% free float operating under an HKEX waiver (a liquidity cost, not business risk); cyclicality and fuel risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not here. Same WACC in every scenario.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A) leases-as-debt. All HKFRS 16 lease liabilities (HK$26,676m at FY2025: 16,216 'with asset transfer' i.e. financed aircraft purchases, 10,460 'without asset transfer' i.e. true operating leases) are inside total_debt and net debt. Lease principal and interest are therefore NOT deducted from the flows; instead the capex path includes right-of-use additions (FY2025 PPE/intangible payments 9,830 + ROU additions 1,273 = 11,103, 9.5% of revenue; FY2024 9,207 + 1,587 = 10.3%) so fleet renewal acquired by lease is still charged. D&A includes ROU depreciation (3,253 FY2025) consistently. Note: the parser's 'HK$10-20bn/yr of lease repayments' reading came from the cash-flow line 'Loan repayments and principal elements of lease payments' (19,683 FY2025), which is mostly loan repayment; lease principal alone is ~HK$4bn/yr (current portion 3,732-4,314) and lease interest 1,305. Under (A) neither is a flow deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is immaterial (profit share HK$0-1m/yr since FY2019; NCI equity HK$7m). Ignored in both flows and bridge.
inputs.associates_treatment: EBITDA (operating profit before net finance charges + D&A; FY2025 14,987 + 11,570 = 26,557, ties to the 26,562 series) EXCLUDES share of associates' results (FY2025 +529, H1 2026 +440 plus a ~HK$1.4bn non-cash deemed-disposal gain from the Air China dilution). Associate income and dividends (376 FY2025) are left out of the flows; the stakes enter the equity bridge at value instead (matching-asset rule).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company) with the non-US/cyclical adaptations: HKD-built WACC, single lease treatment (A), SBC-zero (band collapses, band_position null), associates in the bridge not the flows, risk charged once. Cathay is an operating airline, not a holdco/bank/REIT, so the routing table sends it to owner-FCF. NORMALISATION: FY2020-22 (COVID trough, HK$21.9bn FY2020 loss, HK$19.5bn government preference shares since fully redeemed) and FY2023 (post-reopening yield spike, 29% EBITDA margin) are excluded as anchors. FY2025 owner FCF = OCF 25,381 - capex 9,830 = 15,551 (reported; no SBC, interest income not stripped because the company is net-debt). Forward EBITDA margins glide from ~20.5% (H1 FY2026 actual 20.3% under the fuel shock; FY2025 22.7%, FY2024 25.3%) to a 19% mid-cycle level, deliberately below the 2023-25 run because those years combined post-COVID capacity scarcity with benign fuel; FY2019 (pre-COVID, protest-hit) was 17.3% on the same HKFRS 16 basis. CAPEX: the ~HK$150bn committed fleet/cabin/lounge/digital programme (103+ aircraft on order, 150 new aircraft targeted over 10 years) is charged as a capex hump of 12-12.5% of revenue in FY2027-29 before easing to ~10.5%, above D&A through the horizon. WORKING CAPITAL: airline sales-in-advance (deferred revenue 21.8bn FY2025, 25.7bn June 2026, ~19% of revenue) release cash as revenue grows; captured at 10% of incremental revenue, below the ~19% balance-sheet ratio because other payables/receivables partly offset. Cash tax HK profits tax 16.5% (FY2025 cash tax paid 1,449, ~12% of operating PBT ex associates), ramped 15% -> 16.5%. HK Express is treated as an unproven turnaround: its FY2025 HK$996m loss is inside the base margin and no separate profit swing is credited in base; bull credits it reaching breakeven-plus. Fuel: FY2026 margin in base reflects H1's 59% net-fuel increase partly offset by surcharges; bear assumes the Middle East shock persists through FY2027.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All standard windows are distorted by COVID: 3yr/5yr revenue CAGRs (31.8%/20.0%) measure recovery off the FY2020-22 trough, EPS 3yr/5yr start from losses (undefined), and equity CAGRs (-2.0%/-3.9%) are depressed by the HK$19.5bn government preference shares counted in FY2020-22 equity and redeemed FY2023-24. Book-value CAGR is therefore unusable as the primary rate; the through-cycle FY2019-FY2025 revenue CAGR (1.5%) is selected as the honest long-run proxy. Forward growth in the scenarios is driven by guided ~10% FY2026 capacity growth and HKIA third-runway expansion, not by any of these trailing rates.
historical_growth.notes: SBC is zero, so owner FCF = reported FCF and the FCF CAGRs are on a consistent basis. FCF 3yr (FY2022-25) 3.3%; FY2022 FCF was flattered by recovery working capital (forward sales rebuild).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +18%: H1 +25.3% (passenger +27%, cargo +23% on yields and fuel surcharges) and H2 assumed ~+15% on H2 FY2025's HK$62.5bn as surcharge-driven yield comps harden. FY2027 +6% as ~8-10% capacity growth meets surcharge normalisation; fades to 3% with HKIA three-runway growth tapering.
base.terminal_cap_rationale: 10x terminal FCF cap for a highly cyclical, capital-intensive airline (method allows 12-15x for cyclicals; airlines warrant the low end). Gordon at 8.5%/2.5% would be ~17x, so the cap binds.

scenario_narratives.base: Cathay delivers its guided ~10% FY2026 capacity growth; the Middle East fuel spike compresses FY2026 EBITDA margin to ~20.5% (H1 actual 20.3%) with surcharges recovering part of it, then margins settle at a 19% mid-cycle level as HKIA's third runway invites more competing capacity and the post-COVID yield premium fades. Cargo holds up on AI/data-centre and e-commerce freight but does not repeat the H1 2026 +18% yield. HK Express stays a small drag (no turnaround credited). The HK$150bn fleet programme lifts capex to 12-12.5% of revenue in FY2027-29, above D&A, so owner FCF dips before recovering. Air China and Air China Cargo stakes are valued in the bridge, not projected.
scenario_narratives.bull: Fuel normalises by early 2027 and surcharges hold long enough to protect yields; HKIA's three-runway capacity lets Cathay capture a disproportionate share of hub growth (Seattle, Munich, Brussels, Almaty and further new routes fill well); HK Express turns sustainably profitable after the Pratt & Whitney groundings resolve and it expands to Japan/Vietnam; cargo yields stay elevated on high-value tech freight; Asia Miles/Lifestyle grows as a higher-margin stream. EBITDA margin holds ~22%, close to the FY2024-25 run, and growth runs a point or two above base.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Middle East fuel shock persists through FY2027 while demand softens: surcharges stop sticking, FY2027 revenue is flat and EBITDA margin falls to ~16.5% before settling at 17% (near the FY2019 pre-COVID 17.3%). Greater Bay Area airports, Gulf and mainland carriers and regional LCCs add capacity into Hong Kong, compressing premium yields; HK Express losses persist; cargo yields normalise from the AI-freight peak. The fleet programme is already committed so capex cannot be cut quickly, and FCF is squeezed hardest in FY2027-29. Single-hub concentration and Hong Kong's status as an aviation gateway are the tail risks behind this case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: earnings are at or near a cyclical high after three strong post-COVID years, an unresolved fuel shock is live in H2 2026, capex is committed into a downturn if one comes, and airlines have a long record of giving back peak-cycle margins. Base 50% is the guided capacity path at a mid-cycle margin. Bull cut to 20% because it needs several independent things at once (fuel relief, held yields, HK Express turnaround, sustained cargo yields).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Cathay is valued as a cyclical operating airline on mid-cycle owner FCF, not on the FY2023-25 recovery peak. Leases are treated as debt (all HK$26.7bn of lease liabilities in net debt, lease-funded aircraft additions inside capex), the committed HK$150bn fleet programme is charged as a multi-year capex hump, and the Air China / Air China Cargo stakes are added at the lower of market and book rather than projected through volatile, three-months-in-arrears associate income. Risk is charged once: cyclicality and fuel sit in a 30%-weighted bear case and a 10x terminal cap, with a single 8.5% HKD WACC across scenarios.
key_risks_to_valuation: Fuel: jet fuel is ~30% of opex; H1 2026 net fuel cost rose 59%. Each 1pp of mid-cycle EBITDA margin is worth roughly HK$1/share.
Mid-cycle margin judgment: 19% base sits between FY2019's 17.3% and FY2024-25's 23-25%; if the post-COVID level is structural, base is too low, if FY2019 is the norm it is too high.
Capex programme: HK$150bn committed over roughly a decade; overruns or faster delivery timing push FCF down in the hump years.
Associate stakes: Air China Cargo is carried at book (~HK$6.5bn) against a Dec-2025 quoted value of ~HK$16.9bn; marking it to market would add ~HK$1.7/share.
Liquidity: ~20.5% free float under an HKEX waiver; index eligibility and trading liquidity could weigh on the multiple irrespective of fundamentals.
